extracted.intended_audience: legal professionals (large & small law firms, corporate legal departments, insurers, courts & judges, state & local government, federal government, law schools)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or selecting a legal-analytics platform (Lex Machina) by assessing its data coverage, analytics features, AI assistance, practice-specific metrics, API capabilities, and suitability for litigation strategy and business development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative Analytics / Protégé in Lex Machina
rubrics_metrics.description: Protégé in Lex Machina: intuitive, AI-powered assistance built on high-quality, structured Legal Analytics; allows users to 'simply enter a prompt' to quickly access complex data for actionable intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the feature as enabling faster access to complex data via prompts; implies evaluation on ease-of-use, prompt responsiveness, and accuracy of AI-assisted attorney review. No explicit anti-patterns, but marketing implies reliance on high-quality structured analytics under the hood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Analytics (data science applied to law)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gain insights into the past behavior of parties, counsel, experts, judges, and courts to improve litigation and business outcomes; goes beyond the docket, revealing judge’s specific findings, awarded damages, case resolutions, involved parties, timelines, and much more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate breadth/depth of insights (party/counsel/expert/judge behavior), specificity (judge's findings, damages), and ability to inform strategy. Implies criteria: completeness of extracted findings, linkage to outcomes, and usability for decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive Court Database (coverage & scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage claims: 45M customer-facing documents, over ten million cases, 8K+ judges, 6K+ expert witnesses, 146M+ counsel and 149M+ party mentions; includes all 94 federal district courts, 13 courts of appeal, PTAB, specialty venues, and various enhanced state courts (plus 18M state cases for party analytics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these quantitative coverage metrics to assess comprehensiveness and representativeness. Evaluate currency (dates of coverage), court/venue depth, and whether the jurisdictions and record types needed for a practice area are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Entity Analytics (enriched case/data linking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhanced case data detailing law firms, attorneys, parties, and judges; proprietary AI analyzes documents (including reading signature blocks), updates case data, and groups related entities to show timelines and relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess entity resolution accuracy, ability to group related entities (e.g., related parties or counsel across matters), and correctness of timeline/relationship construction. Important for business intelligence and conflict/relationship analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Court Motion Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Document-driven state court motion metrics focused on orders to access motion practice and timing analytics for over 40+ motion types by judge and court to capture key outcomes and enhance judge analytics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate coverage of motion types relevant to practice, granularity by judge/court, reliance on orders vs. docket events, and whether timing/outcome metrics are detailed enough for motion strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing Events (milestone timing analytics)
rubrics_metrics.description: See how long it takes courts to reach key milestones in cases like yours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure usefulness for case timeline forecasting: availability of milestone definitions, sample sizes, breakdowns by judge/court/case type, and ability to filter for comparable matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Findings (practice-specific findings linked to judgments)
rubrics_metrics.description: View detailed practice-specific legal findings linked to judgment events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the extraction and linking quality of findings to judgment events, coverage across practice areas, and how findings are categorized and searchable for precedent/argument support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals Analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed analytics, information, and documents for all civil cases filed in federal appellate courts since 2012; discover reversal rates revealing outcomes from re-hearings and U.S. Supreme Court decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate scope (since 2012), availability of reversal-rate metrics, depth of appellate documents, and usefulness for appellate-strategy decisions (e.g., predicting reversal likelihood).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class Action Analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use class action analytics to view settlement damages, attorney fees, and class representative awards; summarize timelines to forecast litigation budgets and manage client expectations effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the granularity and reliability of monetary metrics (settlements, fees, awards), ability to segment by industry/issue, and utility for budget forecasting and client management.

rubrics_metrics.name: API Integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate our API to quickly leverage the industry’s most accurate litigation data to create your own solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate API availability, endpoints (data types exposed), latency, documentation, authentication, licensing terms, and whether the API supports required integrations or analytics pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Use Cases / User Needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed for legal professionals to leverage analytics for smarter, data-driven decisions — e.g., crafting legislation, assessing outside counsel, prospecting for clients, optimizing case strategies, managing risks, predicting outcomes, and gaining a competitive edge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the product by how well it supports these workflows: prospecting/business development, counsel selection, litigation strategy, risk management, and forecasting. Assess feature-to-use-case mapping and practical utility in daily workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust / Adoption & Third-Party Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Trusted by over 90% of the largest firms (based on data as of April 2025) and recognized with awards (LEGALTECH BREAKTHROUGH AWARD 2025; 2025 CODiE Awards including Best Data Analytics & Insight Solution and Best AI Tool for Lawyers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use adoption and awards as supporting evidence for product credibility, but corroborate with direct evaluation (trial/demo) and references. Consider recency and applicability of awards to specific practice needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Accuracy and Storytelling Caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimonial warning: 'Be careful when you pitch. Lex Machina is changing the game. If you are less than accurate with your story, and your competitors or your client has access to legal analytics, someone will call you out.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied criterion: analytics must be accurate and defensible; users should validate outputs before relying on them in pitches or court. Evaluate provenance, auditability, and ability to reproduce the analytics behind any claim.
